subject: Capacity upshift plan, governance checklist, and invoice timing
messages:
From: Ethan Rogers <ethan@fluxshop.com>
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-20 09:12 PST
Subject: Planning a commit increase for holiday peak

Hey Maya,

We ran the numbers for the November spike and expect our token usage to run ~3.2x vs our current monthly commit. We want to talk about moving to the next committed tier for Dec–Feb and also understand how soft-throttle + burst pockets will behave for unpredictable peaks.

Can you send over a recommended uplift plan, projected invoices, and any gating/guardrails we should expect? Procurement will need a PDF proposal to kick off approvals.

Thanks — Ethan
Ethan Rogers
Head of Platform, FluxShop
ethan@fluxshop.com

(Phone: +1 415 555 0123)

From: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com
To: Ethan Rogers <ethan@fluxshop.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-20 10:05 PST
Subject: Re: Planning a commit increase for holiday peak

Hi Ethan —

Thanks for the heads-up. Attached is a short proposal (FluxShop_Uplift_Proposal_v3.pdf) that outlines three candidate paths: a conservative +25% commit, an operative +100% commit for predictable coverage, and a staged ramp (50% now, +50% in Jan). For each path we included: monthly cost, burst pocket size, expected token latency impact, and recommended soft-throttle thresholds.

Notes/high level: 
- If you need consistent latency SLAs for checkout-path queries, the +100% commit is the only option that avoids soft-throttle risk for sustained loads above current levels.
- For the staged ramp we recommend enabling automatic burst pocket rollover to avoid urgent credit requests.
- We included an optional SLA sideletter to tighten 95th/99th percentile latency targets for the checkout route — draft attached.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick call today or tomorrow to pick the path (15–20 min).
2) We'll issue a formal quote + DocuSign envelope once you confirm the path and PO terms.
3) Ben (cc) will coordinate provisioning/ops checklist; Karthik (cc) will confirm any region/hardware preferences if you require Dedicated routing.

When is your procurement team available? If you want, I can prepare the DocuSign envelope with the staged ramp terminology and prorated invoice timing for November.

Best,
Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.com
(415) 555-0199

Attachments: FluxShop_Uplift_Proposal_v3.pdf, SLA_sideletter_draft.docx

From: Ethan Rogers <ethan@fluxshop.com>
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com
Cc: Amanda Chu <amanda.chu@fluxshop.com>, FluxShop Procurement <procurement@fluxshop.com>
Date: 2026-11-21 08:44 PST
Subject: Re: Planning a commit increase for holiday peak

Maya —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the options. Amanda in procurement is cc'd. We want the staged ramp: 50% uplift starting Dec 1, then +50% on Jan 15 (to cover peak). Procurement asked: how will invoices be prorated for Dec (since we sign mid-cycle), and can we get the DocuSign today so we can start routing the PO?

Also a couple of ops questions:
- Will the burst pocket be billed only on overage or is it prepaid?
- If we hit soft-throttle on the checkout route, will requests be queued or fail open to a cheaper model? We need behavior that won't break transactions.

Thanks — Ethan

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-22 11:07 PST
Subject: Re: Capacity upshift plan, governance checklist, and invoice timing

Looping in operational details for the staged ramp. Quick answers for procurement + ops so Maya can finalize the DocuSign: 

- Burst pocket model: FluxShop will get a prepaid burst pocket option (recommended) or a post-pay overage. Prepaid burst gives predictability; we'll size the pocket per the proposal (we suggested 20% of monthly commit for Dec as a conservative buffer).
- Billing/proration: If the contract starts mid-billing cycle we prorate the first invoice based on the start date. For staged ramps the Jan 15 increase will be reflected pro rata for that month. We'll include a line-item breakdown in the quote so procurement can map to the PO.
- Soft-throttle behavior: Soft-throttle will never return errors on checkout routes. For route-configured SLOs (which you requested), we will: (a) route to reserved capacity where possible, (b) if reserved capacity is saturated, fall back to a narrower model variant kept warm for fallbacks, and (c) only return a queued/non-blocking delay rather than hard errors. We can document exact fallback model names in the SLA sideletter.

Ben
Ben Carter
Renewals & Expansion, Redwood Inference

Action items: Maya to send DocuSign envelope + final quote; Ops to confirm pocket sizing and record fallback model names in SLA sideletter.

Maya
